fullPassage: Emotion socialization — learning from other people about emotions and how to deal with them — starts early in life and plays a foundational role for emotion regulation development. Although extra-familial influences, such as peers or media, gain in importance during adolescence, parents remain the primary socialization agents. For example, their own responses to emotional situations serve as a role model for emotion regulation, increasing the likelihood that their children will show similar reactions in comparable situations. Parental practices at times when their children are faced with emotional challenges also impact emotion regulation development. Whereas direct soothing and directive guidance of what to do are beneficial for younger children, they may frustrate adolescents' autonomy striving. In consequence, adolescents might pull away from, rather than turn toward, their parents in times of emotional crisis, unless parental practices are adjusted. More suitable in adolescence is indirect support of autonomous emotion regulation, such as through interest in, as well as awareness and nonjudgmental acceptance of, adolescents' emotional experiences, and being available when the adolescent wants to talk. Free play is nature's means of teaching children that they are not helpless. In play, away from adults, children really do have control and can practice asserting it. In free play, children learn to make their own decisions, solve their own problems, create and follow rules, and get along with others as equals rather than as obedient or rebellious subordinates. In active outdoor play, children deliberately dose themselves with moderate amounts of fear and they thereby learn how to control not only their bodies, but also their fear. In social play children learn how to negotiate with others, how to please others, and how to manage and overcome the anger that can arise from conflicts. None of these lessons can be taught through verbal means; they can be learned only through experience, which free play provides. Technologists are always on the lookout for quantifiable metrics. Measurable inputs to a model are their lifeblood, and like a social scientist, a technologist needs to identify concrete measures, or "proxies," for assessing progress. This need for quantifiable proxies produces a bias toward measuring things that are easy to quantify. But simple metrics can take us further away from the important goals we really care about, which may require complicated metrics or be extremely difficult, or perhaps impossible, to reduce to any measure. And when we have imperfect or bad proxies, we can easily fall under the illusion that we are solving for a good end without actually making genuine progress toward a worthy solution. The problem of proxies results in technologists frequently substituting what is measurable for what is meaningful. As the saying goes, "Not everything that counts can be counted, and not everything that can be counted counts." Information encountered after an event can influence subsequent remembering. External information can easily integrate into a witness's memory, especially if the event was poorly encoded or the memory is from a distant event, in which case time and forgetting have degraded the original memory. With reduced information available in memory with which to confirm the validity of post-event misinformation, it is less likely that this new information will be rejected. Instead, especially when it fits the witness's current thinking and can be used to create a story that makes sense to him or her, it may be integrated as part of the original experience. This process can be explicit (i.e., the witness knows it is happening), but it is often unconscious. That is, the witness might find himself or herself thinking about the event differently without awareness. Over time, the witness may not even know the source of information that led to the (new) memory. Sources of misinformation in forensic contexts can be encountered anywhere, from discussions with other witnesses to social media searches to multiple interviews with investigators or other legal professionals, and even in court. Correlations are powerful because the insights they offer are relatively clear. These insights are often covered up when we bring causality back into the picture. For instance, a used-car dealer supplied data to statisticians to predict which of the vehicles available for purchase at an auction were likely to have problems. A correlation analysis showed that orange-colored cars were far less likely to have defects. Even as we read this, we already think about why it might be so: Are orange-colored car owners likely to be car enthusiasts and take better care of their vehicles? Or, is it because orange-colored cars are more noticeable on the road and therefore less likely to be in accidents, so they're in better condition when resold? Quickly we are caught in a web of competing causal hypotheses. But our attempts to illuminate things this way only make them cloudier. Correlations exist; we can show them mathematically. We can't easily do the same for causal links. So we would do well to hold off from trying to explain the reason behind the correlations. Much of human thought is designed to screen out information and to sort the rest into a manageable condition. The inflow of data from our senses could create an overwhelming chaos, especially given the enormous amount of information available in culture and society. Out of all the sensory impressions and possible information, it is vital to find a small amount that is most relevant to our individual needs and to organize that into a usable stock of knowledge. Expectancies accomplish some of this work, helping to screen out information that is irrelevant to what is expected, and focusing our attention on clear contradictions. The processes of learning and memory are marked by a steady elimination of information. People notice only a part of the world around them. Then, only a fraction of what they notice gets processed and stored into memory. And only part of what gets committed to memory can be retrieved. Many people look for safety and security in popular thinking. They figure that if a lot of people are doing something, then it must be right. It must be a good idea. If most people accept it, then it probably represents fairness, equality, compassion, and sensitivity, right? Not necessarily. Popular thinking said the earth was the center of the universe, yet Copernicus studied the stars and planets and proved mathematically that the earth and the other planets in our solar system revolved around the sun. Popular thinking said surgery didn't require clean instruments, yet Joseph Lister studied the high death rates in hospitals and introduced antiseptic practices that immediately saved lives. Popular thinking said that women shouldn't have the right to vote, yet people like Emmeline Pankhurst and Susan B. Anthony fought for and won that right. We must always remember there is a huge difference between acceptance and intelligence. People may say that there's safety in numbers, but that's not always true. If you drive down a busy street, you will find many competing businesses, often right next to one another. For example, in most places a consumer in search of a quick meal has many choices, and more fast-food restaurants appear all the time. These competing firms advertise heavily. The temptation is to see advertising as driving up the price of a product without any benefit to the consumer. However, this misconception doesn't account for why firms advertise. In markets where competitors sell slightly differentiated products, advertising enables firms to inform their customers about new products and services. Yes, costs rise, but consumers also gain information to help make purchasing decisions. Consumers also benefit from added variety, and we all get a product that's pretty close to our vision of a perfect good — and no other market structure delivers that outcome. Intuition can be great, but it ought to be hard-earned. Experts, for example, are able to think on their feet because they've invested thousands of hours in learning and practice: their intuition has become data-driven. Only then are they able to act quickly in accordance with their internalized expertise and evidence-based experience. Yet most people are not experts, though they often think they are. Most of us, especially when we interact with others on social media, act with expert-like speed and conviction, offering a wide range of opinions on global crises, without the substance of knowledge that supports it. And thanks to AI, which ensures that our messages are delivered to an audience more inclined to believing it, our delusions of expertise can be reinforced by our personal filter bubble. We have an interesting tendency to find people more open-minded, rational, and sensible when they think just like us. Electric communication is mainly known in fish. The electric signals are produced in special electric organs. When the signal is discharged the electric organ will be negatively loaded compared to the head and an electric field is created around the fish. A weak electric current is created also in ordinary muscle cells when they contract. In the electric organ the muscle cells are connected in larger chunks, which makes the total current intensity larger than in ordinary muscles. The fish varies the signals by changing the form of the electric field or the frequency of discharging. The system is only working over small distances, about one to two meters. This is an advantage since the species using the signal system often live in large groups with several other species. If many fish send out signals at the same time, the short range decreases the risk of interference.

✅ ① beneficial — frustrate — indirect: 세 자리 모두 원문과 일치하는 정답.
❌ ② harmful — frustrate — direct: (A) harmful, (C) direct가 문맥 역행.
❌ ③ beneficial — satisfy — indirect: (B) satisfy가 대조 구조에 어긋남.

(B) saved(구했다) ↔ lost(잃게 했다): 소독법이 즉시 생명을 구했다가 맞다.

✅ ② proved — saved — difference: 세 자리 모두 원문과 일치하는 정답.
❌ ③ proved — lost — difference: (B) lost가 문맥 역행.
❌ ④ proved — saved — similarity: (C) similarity가 대조 취지에 반함.
det.tip: 각 사례가 대중적 통념을 '뒤집는' 방향인지 확인하면 낱말이 결정된다.

❌ ① vague — defects — cloudier: (A) vague가 논지와 반대.

det.korean: 아이들이 스스로를 조절하는 법을 배우는 자유 놀이의 이점을 다루며, 아이들은 '적당한(moderate)' 양의 두려움을 스스로에게 부여한다는 것이 원문이다.

① control(통제력) — 아이들이 실제로 통제력을 갖고 그것을 발휘하는 연습을 한다는 원문 흐름에 맞다.

② decisions(결정) — 스스로 결정을 내리는 법을 배운다는 자연스러운 표현이다.

③ extreme(극단적인) — 원문은 아이들이 스스로에게 'moderate(적당한)' 양의 두려움을 부여한다이다. extreme(극단적인)은 스스로 조절 가능한 수준이라는 맥락과 정반대이므로 부적절하다. (정답)

④ overcome(극복하다) — 갈등에서 생기는 분노를 관리하고 극복하는 법을 배운다는 흐름에 맞다.

따라서 문맥상 부적절한 것은 ③번이다.
det.tip: '스스로 조절 가능한 두려움'이라는 취지상 extreme는 논리적으로 어긋난다.

④ lose(잃다) — 원문은 소비자가 구매 결정을 돕는 정보를 'gain(얻는다)'이다. lose(잃다)는 소비자가 이득을 본다는 글 전체 논지와 정반대이므로 부적절하다. (정답)

det.korean: 일반 근육 세포가 '수축할(contract)' 때 약한 전류가 만들어진다는 내용이다.

① organized(조직화된) — 걸러내야 할 대상은 조직화된 것이 아니라 혼돈이므로 맞지 않는다.

② limited(제한된) — 뒤에 chaos(혼돈)와 enormous amount(막대한 양)가 이어져 '제한된'과 모순된다.

③ overwhelming(압도적인) — 막대한 정보가 압도적인 혼돈을 만들 수 있다는 원문 흐름에 맞으므로 정답이다.

④ pleasant(유쾌한) — 걸러내야 할 부정적 상황과 어울리지 않는다.

따라서 정답은 ③번이다.
det.tip: chaos, enormous amount 등 부정적/과다한 어휘가 overwhelming을 가리킨다.

questions.passage: Information encountered after an event can influence subsequent remembering. External information can easily integrate into a witness's memory, especially if the event was poorly encoded or the memory is from a distant event, in which case time and forgetting have degraded the original memory. With reduced information available in memory with which to confirm the validity of post-event misinformation, it is less likely that this new information will be __________. Instead, especially when it fits the witness's current thinking and can be used to create a story that makes sense to him or her, it may be integrated as part of the original experience. This process can be explicit (i.e., the witness knows it is happening), but it is often unconscious. That is, the witness might find himself or herself thinking about the event differently without awareness. Over time, the witness may not even know the source of information that led to the (new) memory. Sources of misinformation in forensic contexts can be encountered anywhere, from discussions with other witnesses to social media searches to multiple interviews with investigators or other legal professionals, and even in court.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 기억 속 정보가 부족하면 사후 오정보가 '거부될(rejected)' 가능성이 낮아진다는 내용이다.
det.analysis:
① accepted(받아들여진) — 문장은 오정보가 받아들여지기 쉬워진다는 취지이나, 빈칸 자리 동사는 부정될 가능성을 말하므로 accepted는 어색하다.

② rejected(거부된) — 확인할 정보가 줄면 새 정보가 거부될 가능성이 낮아진다는 원문 흐름에 정확히 맞으므로 정답이다.

③ doubted(의심된) — 의미는 유사하나 원문 어휘가 아니며, 이어지는 integrate와의 논리 연결이 rejected만큼 명확하지 않다.

④ verified(검증된) — 검증은 오정보가 통합된다는 뒤 문장과 상충한다.

따라서 정답은 ②번이다.
det.tip: less likely that ~ will be rejected → 거부되기 어려워 오정보가 통합된다는 흐름.

questions.passage: Technologists are always on the lookout for quantifiable metrics. Measurable inputs to a model are their lifeblood, and like a social scientist, a technologist needs to identify concrete measures, or "proxies," for <u>assessing</u> progress. This need for quantifiable proxies produces a bias toward measuring things that are easy to quantify. But simple metrics can take us further away from the important goals we really care about, which may require complicated metrics or be extremely difficult, or perhaps impossible, to reduce to any measure. And when we have imperfect or bad proxies, we can easily fall under the illusion that we are solving for a good end without actually making genuine progress toward a worthy solution. The problem of proxies results in technologists frequently substituting what is measurable for what is meaningful. As the saying goes, "Not everything that counts can be counted, and not everything that can be counted counts."
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 assessing와 의미가 가장 가까운 것은?

det.korean: assessing은 진척을 '평가하다'라는 뜻으로 evaluating과 가장 가깝다.
det.analysis:
① ignoring(무시하다) — 평가와 반대되는 뜻이다.

② delaying(지연시키다) — 시간 지연의 의미로 assess와 무관하다.

③ reducing(줄이다) — 규모 축소의 뜻으로 평가와 다르다.

④ evaluating(평가하다) — assessing progress(진척을 평가하다)와 동일한 의미이므로 정답이다.

따라서 정답은 ④번이다.
det.tip: assess = evaluate = judge, 진척·성과를 '가늠하다'.

questions.passage: Intuition can be great, but it ought to be hard-earned. Experts, for example, are able to think on their feet because they've invested thousands of hours in learning and practice: their intuition has become data-driven. Only then are they able to act quickly in accordance with their internalized expertise and evidence-based experience. Yet most people are not experts, though they often think they are. Most of us, especially when we interact with others on social media, act with expert-like speed and <u>conviction</u>, offering a wide range of opinions on global crises, without the substance of knowledge that supports it. And thanks to AI, which ensures that our messages are delivered to an audience more inclined to believing it, our delusions of expertise can be reinforced by our personal filter bubble. We have an interesting tendency to find people more open-minded, rational, and sensible when they think just like us.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 conviction와 의미가 가장 가까운 것은?

det.korean: conviction은 여기서 '확신'의 뜻으로 certainty와 가장 가깝다.
det.analysis:
① certainty(확신) — 전문가처럼 빠른 속도와 확신을 갖고 행동한다는 맥락에서 conviction과 동일한 의미이므로 정답이다.

② hesitation(주저) — 확신과 반대되는 뜻이다.

③ curiosity(호기심) — 의미가 전혀 다르다.

④ patience(인내) — 문맥과 무관한 뜻이다.

따라서 정답은 ①번이다.
det.tip: speed and conviction = 빠름과 '확신'. conviction의 '유죄판결' 뜻과 혼동 주의.

questions.passage: Correlations are powerful because the insights they offer are relatively clear. These insights are often covered up when we bring causality back into the picture. For instance, a used-car dealer supplied data to statisticians to predict which of the vehicles available for purchase at an auction were likely to have problems. A correlation analysis showed that orange-colored cars were far less likely to have defects. Even as we read this, we already think about why it might be so: Are orange-colored car owners likely to be car enthusiasts and take better care of their vehicles? Or, is it because orange-colored cars are more noticeable on the road and therefore less likely to be in accidents, so they're in better condition when resold? Quickly we are caught in a web of competing causal hypotheses. But our attempts to <u>illuminate</u> things this way only make them cloudier. Correlations exist; we can show them mathematically. We can't easily do the same for causal links. So we would do well to hold off from trying to explain the reason behind the correlations.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 illuminate와 의미가 가장 가까운 것은?

det.korean: illuminate는 여기서 '분명히 밝히다'의 뜻으로 clarify와 가장 가깝다.
det.analysis:
① complicate(복잡하게 하다) — 결과적으로 흐려진다는 뒤 내용과 관련되지만, illuminate 자체의 의도된 의미('밝히다')와는 반대다.

② conceal(숨기다) — 밝히려는 시도라는 의미와 정반대다.

③ clarify(명확히 하다) — 상황을 밝혀 설명하려는 시도라는 맥락에서 illuminate와 동일하므로 정답이다.

④ ignore(무시하다) — 설명하려는 행위와 무관하다.

따라서 정답은 ③번이다.
det.tip: illuminate things = 이해를 '밝히다/명료하게 하다' = clarify.

questions.passage: Emotion socialization — learning from other people about emotions and how to deal with them — starts early in life and plays a foundational role for emotion regulation development. Although extra-familial influences, such as peers or media, gain in importance during adolescence, parents remain the <u>primary</u> socialization agents. For example, their own responses to emotional situations serve as a role model for emotion regulation, increasing the likelihood that their children will show similar reactions in comparable situations. Parental practices at times when their children are faced with emotional challenges also impact emotion regulation development. Whereas direct soothing and directive guidance of what to do are beneficial for younger children, they may frustrate adolescents' autonomy striving. In consequence, adolescents might pull away from, rather than turn toward, their parents in times of emotional crisis, unless parental practices are adjusted. More suitable in adolescence is indirect support of autonomous emotion regulation, such as through interest in, as well as awareness and nonjudgmental acceptance of, adolescents' emotional experiences, and being available when the adolescent wants to talk.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 primary와 의미가 가장 먼 것은?

det.korean: primary는 '주된, 일차적인'의 뜻으로 반대말은 secondary(부차적인)이다.
det.analysis:
① main(주된) — primary의 동의어이므로 반의어가 아니다.

② secondary(부차적인) — '일차적인'과 반대되는 뜻이므로 정답이다.

③ chief(주요한) — primary와 유사한 뜻이다.

④ leading(선도적인) — primary와 유사한 뜻이다.

따라서 의미가 가장 먼 것은 ②번이다.
det.tip: primary ↔ secondary. 나머지 셋은 모두 '주된'의 동의어.

questions.passage: Much of human thought is designed to screen out information and to sort the rest into a manageable condition. The inflow of data from our senses could create an overwhelming chaos, especially given the enormous amount of information available in culture and society. Out of all the sensory impressions and possible information, it is <u>vital</u> to find a small amount that is most relevant to our individual needs and to organize that into a usable stock of knowledge. Expectancies accomplish some of this work, helping to screen out information that is irrelevant to what is expected, and focusing our attention on clear contradictions. The processes of learning and memory are marked by a steady elimination of information. People notice only a part of the world around them. Then, only a fraction of what they notice gets processed and stored into memory. And only part of what gets committed to memory can be retrieved.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 vital와 의미가 가장 먼 것은?

det.korean: vital은 '필수적인, 매우 중요한'의 뜻으로 반대말은 trivial(사소한)이다.
det.analysis:
① trivial(사소한) — '필수적인'과 정반대의 뜻이므로 정답이다.

② essential(필수적인) — vital의 동의어이므로 반의어가 아니다.

③ crucial(결정적으로 중요한) — vital과 유사한 뜻이다.

④ necessary(필요한) — vital과 유사한 뜻이다.

따라서 의미가 가장 먼 것은 ①번이다.
det.tip: vital ↔ trivial. 나머지 셋은 '중요한/필수적인'으로 vital의 동의어.

questions.passage:
(A) A weak electric <u>current</u> is created also in ordinary muscle cells when they contract. In the electric organ the muscle cells are connected in larger chunks, which makes the total current intensity larger than in ordinary muscles.

(B) External information can easily integrate into a witness's memory. Especially when it fits the witness's <u>current</u> thinking and can be used to create a story that makes sense to him or her, it may be integrated as part of the original experience.
questions.stem: 다음 (A), (B)의 밑줄 친 current의 문맥적 의미로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: (A)의 current는 근육 세포에서 만들어지는 '전류'(명사)이고, (B)의 current는 목격자의 '현재의' 사고를 가리키는 형용사이다.
det.analysis:
(A) electric current는 muscle cells가 만들어내는 것이므로 '전류'라는 명사 의미다.

(B) current thinking은 '현재의 사고'라는 형용사 의미다.

❌ ① (A) 현재의 — (B) 전류: 두 항목이 모두 뒤바뀌어 있어 오답이다.

❌ ② (A) 해류 — (B) 최신의: (A)는 전류이지 해류가 아니므로 오답이다.

❌ ③ (A) 전류 — (B) 흐르는: (B)는 '흐르는'이 아니라 '현재의'이므로 오답이다.

✅ ④ (A) 전류 — (B) 현재의: 두 문맥의 의미가 모두 정확하므로 정답이다.

따라서 정답은 ④번이다.
det.tip: current는 명사 '전류/해류/흐름'과 형용사 '현재의' 두 갈래. 앞뒤 명사·수식 관계로 구분하라.

questions.stem: 다음 영영 풀이가 설명하는 단어로 가장 적절한 것은? "a mutual relationship or connection between two or more things, especially one in which a change in one is associated with a change in another"

det.korean: 두 대상 사이의 상호 관계, 특히 한쪽의 변화가 다른 쪽 변화와 연관되는 것을 뜻하는 단어는 correlation(상관관계)이다.
det.analysis:
① causation(인과관계) — 한쪽이 다른 쪽을 '유발'하는 관계로, 단순 연관을 뜻하는 풀이와 다르다.

② correlation(상관관계) — 두 대상의 변화가 함께 연관되는 상호 관계라는 풀이에 정확히 부합하므로 정답이다.

③ coincidence(우연의 일치) — 인과나 규칙적 연관 없이 우연히 겹치는 것으로 풀이와 다르다.

④ comparison(비교) — 두 대상을 견주는 행위로, 변화의 연관을 뜻하는 풀이와 다르다.

따라서 정답은 ②번이다.
det.tip: correlation은 '함께 변하는 연관', causation은 '원인-결과'. 지문의 핵심 대비 개념이다.

questions.passage: The processes of learning and memory are __________ (mark) by a steady elimination of information. People notice only a part of the world around them.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 주어진 단어를 문맥과 어법에 맞게 변형하여 쓰시오. (영어로)

det.korean: 'be동사(are) + 과거분사' 수동태 구조이므로 mark를 과거분사 marked로 바꿔 쓴다.
det.analysis: The processes ~ are __________ by ~ 구조에서 주어(the processes)가 '특징지어지는' 대상이고 be동사 are와 행위자 by가 함께 쓰였으므로 수동태이다. 따라서 원형 mark를 과거분사 marked로 변형해야 한다.
det.tip: 'be + p.p. + by' 형태가 보이면 수동태 → 과거분사로 변형.

questions.passage: Only then are they able to act quickly in accordance with their __________ (internalize) expertise and evidence-based experience. Yet most people are not experts, though they often think they are.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 주어진 단어를 문맥과 어법에 맞게 변형하여 쓰시오. (영어로)

det.korean: 명사 expertise를 앞에서 수식하는 분사형 형용사가 필요하므로 internalize를 과거분사 internalized로 바꿔 쓴다.
det.analysis: their __________ expertise에서 빈칸은 명사 expertise를 수식하는 자리이며, '내면화된 전문성'이라는 수동·완료의 의미가 필요하다. 따라서 원형 internalize를 과거분사 internalized로 변형해 형용사처럼 쓴다.
det.tip: 명사 앞 수식 자리에서 '~된' 의미면 과거분사(-ed)로 변형.

questions.passage: Technologists are always __________ for quantifiable metrics. Measurable inputs to a model are their lifeblood, and like a social scientist, a technologist needs to identify concrete measures, or "proxies," for assessing progress. This need for quantifiable proxies produces a bias toward measuring things that are easy to quantify. But simple metrics can take us further away from the important goals we really care about, which may require complicated metrics or be extremely difficult, or perhaps impossible, to reduce to any measure. And when we have imperfect or bad proxies, we can easily fall under the illusion that we are solving for a good end without actually making genuine progress toward a worthy solution. The problem of proxies results in technologists frequently substituting what is measurable for what is meaningful. As the saying goes, "Not everything that counts can be counted, and not everything that can be counted counts."
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 기술자들은 정량화 가능한 지표를 늘 '찾고 있다(on the lookout)'는 내용이다.
det.analysis:
① in the dark(모르는 상태로) — 지표를 적극적으로 찾는 능동적 태도와 반대다.

② at a loss(어쩔 줄 몰라) — 당혹감을 뜻해 문맥과 맞지 않는다.

③ on the lookout(늘 살피는/찾는) — 기술자들이 정량화 지표를 항상 찾는다는 원문 흐름에 정확히 맞으므로 정답이다.

④ out of touch(동떨어진) — 정보에서 소외된 상태로 문맥과 반대다.

따라서 정답은 ③번이다.
det.tip: always ~ for quantifiable metrics → 무언가를 '늘 찾는' on the lookout for.

questions.passage: Many people look for safety and security in popular thinking. They figure that if a lot of people are doing something, then it must be right. It must be a good idea. If most people accept it, then it probably represents fairness, equality, compassion, and sensitivity, right? Not necessarily. Popular thinking said the earth was the center of the universe, yet Copernicus studied the stars and planets and proved mathematically that the earth and the other planets in our solar system revolved around the sun. Popular thinking said surgery didn't require clean instruments, yet Joseph Lister studied the high death rates in hospitals and introduced antiseptic practices that immediately saved lives. Popular thinking said that women shouldn't have the right to vote, yet people like Emmeline Pankhurst and Susan B. Anthony fought for and won that right. We must always remember there is a huge difference between acceptance and intelligence. People may say that there's __________, but that's not always true.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 사람들은 '다수 속에 안전이 있다(safety in numbers)'고 말하지만 늘 옳은 것은 아니라는 내용이다.
det.analysis:
① safety in numbers(다수 속의 안전) — 대중적 사고에서 안전을 찾는다는 글 전체 논지와, but that's not always true로 이어지는 대조에 정확히 맞으므로 정답이다.

② strength in silence(침묵 속의 힘) — 다수/대중 논지와 관련이 없다.

③ wisdom in age(나이의 지혜) — 나이·경험 관련으로 문맥과 무관하다.

④ truth in power(권력의 진실) — 권력 주제로 글의 다수 논지와 다르다.

따라서 정답은 ①번이다.
det.tip: 글의 주제가 '다수를 따르는 것'이므로 numbers(다수)와 연결된 관용구 safety in numbers가 정답.
